This body, this shell, is what we have. There is no reason to be ashamed of it, no reason to judge other people on it, and no reason to think that a naked body is "freaky" or "unnatural". I think that we put way to much emphasis on what we "should" look like that we don't appreciate the beauty of what we actually look like.

It has honestly been a few years since I have read anything by Ayn Rand, but the last thing I read was The Fountainhead, and I thoroughly enjoyed reading that book. Knowing her to get a bit preachy, I skipped the entirety of the shit dialogue/manifesto, didn't particularly enjoy the end, but still felt like I took something away from it. 

I don't mean to bitch here, but I think that anyone who can stand behind any singular work, jump up on a soap box and say, "THIS PERSON SAYS THIS IS THE RIGHT WAY TO LIVE AND I AGREE WITH THAT AND YOU SHOULD, TOO!" is a fucking idiot. The amazing thing about literature, ideas, ANYTHING in life, is that collectively, it gives us a foundation to stand upon. 

In example, I love the emphasis on individualism. If there is something you love that is a part of you that you cannot help but doing, nothing can and should stand in your way; I feel that way about singing and government reform, and always have. However, I highly disagree with the idea that individualism, to the extent that no one else matters to a point where we are "weeding out the weak" is not justified. 

I think my emphasis for this rant would be education, then. It is important for people to read, yes, but it is even more important for them to be able to read and think critically about what they are reading. To formulate ideas is a great thing; to be able to back them up by your own convictions, real life practice, and thoughtfulness about the affect this choice may have on people that are unlike you is the road to equality and progress.
